course.title: AI Local Buisness ADS
course.description:
AI Local Business Ads
Professional course description
AI Local Business Ads is a practical, beginner-friendly course designed to help small business owners and
aspiring local content creators produce honest, effective marketing assets using accessible AI tools. Through
ten focused lessons, learners move from understanding a business and its customers to creating polished
shop and menu photography, offer and festival posters, short promotional videos, Hindi voiceover reels and
manageable publishing plans.
The course demonstrates how ChatGPT supports business briefs, writing and planning; how Google Flow can
assist with image and video creation; how CapCut brings clips together; and how ElevenLabs can provide an
optional text-to-speech workflow. It also introduces the fundamentals of offering this work as a service to
neighborhood businesses.
What learners will gain
Build a reusable business brief with customer segments, advertising angles and a content calendar.
Improve real shop, food and product photos while preserving their authentic appearance.
Create promotional posters using exact, approved wording and verified prices.
Produce short vertical reels and natural Hindi voiceovers.
Prepare platform-specific content for Instagram, WhatsApp and Google Business Profile.
Package creative services, collect client requirements and manage approvals.
Who this course is for
Owners of cafes, salons, bakeries, neighborhood stores and other local businesses.
Beginners interested in creating AI-assisted marketing content for nearby shops.
Content creators seeking a practical, ethical workflow for small-business clients.

Lesson 01 | Course Introduction
Lesson overview
Understand the end-to-end workflow for creating honest local advertising with AI.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 01 and its place in the course workflow.

videos.notes:
SKILLOMATE  |  Student Lesson Notes1

Lesson 02 | Business Brief with ChatGPT
Lesson overview
Develop customer groups, advertising angles, five potential offers and a 30-day plan from verified facts.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 02 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. In one ChatGPT conversation provide shop category, city, locality, menu, hours and genuine differentiators.
2. Ask for customer groups, typical needs and advertising angles; request five offer ideas with [price]
placeholders; request a 30-day calendar; consolidate into a one-page brief.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
Treat customer timings as estimates unless backed by records. Label unknown facts Not confirmed. Mark
festival dates (check date) and verify independently.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
A generic brief lacking city and locality may produce non-local advertisements. The owner must decide actual
prices and approve offers.
Practical assignment
Create one verified brief with three advertising angles, five offer ideas and a 30-day posting plan.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.
Approved prompt reference (original wording)
Lesson 02 — Business Brief (chat G.P.T, ek hi chat
mein, order se)
Step 1: Details → customers, time, ad angles
I run a small [cafe / salon / bakery / shop] in [area, city]. Details:
- Menu / services: [list]

SKILLOMATE  |  Student Lesson Notes2
- Price range: [₹ – ₹]
- Timing: [opening – closing]
- Seating / size: [if any]
- Who usually comes: [students, office people, families...]
- What's special: [only write what is true]
Make a simple business brief:
1. Types of customers and what time of day they come
2. What each type cares about most
3. One ad angle for each type
Keep it short, in simple Hinglish.
Step 2: 5 offers
Suggest 5 offer ideas for this [shop] that are simple and won't hurt profit much — like
combos, a happy hour, or a student deal. For each one, say who it is for and the best day
or time to run it. Don't decide prices — write [price] wherever the owner should fill it
in.
Step 3: 30 din ka post plan
Make a 30-day post plan for this [shop] starting [date]. For each week, tell me what to
post on Instagram and WhatsApp status — a food/product photo, an offer poster, a short
reel, or a behind-the-counter moment. Include any Indian festivals in these dates and mark
them clearly with "(check date)" so I can verify them.
Step 4: Ek page ka Business Brief
Now put everything into one short Business Brief I can save and reuse: business details,
customer types, 3 ad angles, 5 offers, and the 30-day plan. Clean headings, no extra text.

Lesson 03 | Upgrade Shop Photos
Lesson overview
Improve real interior and storefront phone photos while preserving the shop identity.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 03 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. Upload a genuine photo to Google Flow Image > Nano Banana Pro.
2. Describe lighting, color, straightening and cleanup.
3. Explicitly preserve the furniture, layout, counter, signs and name.
4. Retain the original aspect ratio for the main upgrade; request a separate 9:16 WhatsApp Status variant
with empty top space.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
Inspect the result against the reference: signage, walls, furniture and layout must remain consistent. A
second generation may be necessary.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
A vague instruction such as make it luxurious may add chandeliers, wood panels or chairs that do not exist.
Practical assignment
Create two accurate shop upgrades and a vertical status version; compare each against the original.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.

Lesson 03 — Dukaan Ki Photos (Flow · Image · Nano
Banana Pro)
Andar ki photo upgrade

SKILLOMATE  |  Student Lesson Notes2
Turn this phone photo of my [shop] into a professional interior photograph, like one shot
by a good photographer for Instagram and Google Maps. Keep the same room, same furniture,
same counter, same boards and same layout — do not add or remove any furniture.
Make these improvements boldly:
- Lighting: replace the harsh tube-light look with warm, soft, inviting light
- Colours: rich and warm, clean walls, natural shine on surfaces
- Camera: straighten the photo, fix the tilt and the stretched wide-angle look, frame it
at normal eye level
- Clean-up: tables wiped clean, chairs neatly pushed in, floor clean, remove clutter,
wires and stains
- Quality: sharp focus, no grain, natural depth, looks like a real DSLR photo
No people, no new decorations, no plants, no text added. Realistic, not AI-looking.
Shop front, shaam ka look
Turn this phone photo of my [shop]'s front into a professional evening photograph. Keep
the same building, same door, same chairs outside and the same signboard — the text "[SHOP
NAME]" must stay exactly the same, do not change, re-write or translate it.
Make these improvements boldly:
- Time: early evening, soft deep-blue sky, warm golden light glowing from inside
- Camera: straighten the photo, fix the tilt, frame the shop front centred and balanced
- Clean-up: remove parked vehicles, wrappers and dust, tidy the overhead wires, clean
footpath
- Colours: rich and warm, sharp focus, no grain, looks like a real DSLR photo
No people, no new signs, no new lights or decorations added. Realistic, not AI-looking.
WhatsApp status version (9:16)
Use this [shop] photo. Make a vertical 9:16 version of the same [shop] for WhatsApp status
— same interior, same furniture, nothing new added. Keep clean empty space in the top

Lesson 04 | Menu and Food Photos
Lesson overview
Create polished photos of the same food and drink actually sold.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 04 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. Upload the original dish as a reference, then ask for a new professional re-shoot.
2. Describe the exact dish, plate, ingredients and portion.
3. Choose natural warm lighting and a 45-degree angle.
4. For drinks preserve the glass and toppings.
5. Combine two accurate images into a combo with space for later text.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
A reference should guide what is photographed, not be pasted unchanged onto a new table. Compare each
output with the original menu item.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
Overly vague prompts can invent coriander, cheese, larger portions or additional toppings.
Practical assignment
Create three accurate menu photos, including a combo, and check them against real items.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.
Approved prompt reference (original wording)

Lesson 05 | Offer and Festival Posters
Lesson overview
Make promotional graphics with accurate wording and owner-approved claims.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 05 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. Use a real food or shop photo.
2. For an offer poster supply the exact name, items, price, days, time and shop identity.
3. Ask for ONLY that text.
4. For festival greetings keep decorations around the frame rather than on the physical storefront.
5. Proofread all generated words.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
The ₹99 Chai Kona Student Combo is an example from the course, not a default price for other shops.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
AI may invent Buy 1 Get 1 offers, dates or spelling. Verify every word and price before posting.
Practical assignment
Create one verified offer poster and one festival greeting, and obtain owner approval.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.

Lesson 05 — Posters
Offer poster
Use this photo of our [items] as the main image. Turn it into a clean, modern offer poster
for Instagram for our [shop]. Keep the food exactly as it is in the photo — do not add or

- Top, big bold: "[OFFER NAME]"
- Below it: "[item 1] + [item 2]"
- Big price badge: "₹[price]"
- Small: "[days, time]"
- Bottom: "[SHOP NAME] · [area, city]"
Warm colours, easy-to-read bold fonts, clean layout with the food clearly visible. Do not
add any other words, discounts, percentages, logos or claims.

Lesson 06 | Shop Photos to Video
Lesson overview
Turn three genuine photos into a short vertical reel with restrained motion.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 06 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. In Flow Video > Ingredients use 9:16 and the lesson’s 6-second clip setting.
2. Make a storefront push-in, an interior glide toward the counter and a gentle circle around the food.
3. Preserve the exact board text and scene objects.
4. Download the three clips and join them in CapCut into an 18-second reel.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
One photo should have one gentle movement. Watch all frames for changed menus, prices, furniture or
signboards.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
A generic cinematic prompt may create fake equipment, people, text or prices. Current Flow options can
change; use available settings rather than claiming fixed limits.
Practical assignment
Produce a three-clip 18-second reel and log any visual inaccuracies.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.

videos.title: Hindi Voiceover Reel
videos.notes:
SKILLOMATE  |  Student Lesson Notes1
SKILLOMATE / AI LOCAL BUSINESS ADS
Lesson 07 | Hindi Voiceover Reel
Lesson overview
Write factual Hindi lines and add consistent narration to a short business reel.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 07 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. Ask ChatGPT for three natural Hindi lines in Devanagari, each at most 12 words and easy to speak in six
seconds.
2. For Flow’s lesson example use three 8-second 9:16 clips: 0–1 seconds ambience, 1–7 narration, 7–8
ambience.
3. Keep the same voice description in all clips.
4. Alternatively generate audio with ElevenLabs and edit it onto silent clips in CapCut.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
Lesson 7 uses three 8-second clips (24 seconds), unlike Lesson 6’s three 6-second clips (18 seconds).
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
Listen for changes in voice across clips; do not use unverified best, No.1 or cheapest claims.
Practical assignment
Prepare three Hindi lines and assemble one approved narrated reel.
Student review checklist

Lesson 08 | Where and When to Post
Lesson overview
Plan a manageable publishing routine for Instagram, WhatsApp and Google Business Profile.
Learning objectives
Understand the purpose of Lesson 08 and its place in the course workflow.
Apply the lesson method to a real local business using approved facts.
Review the output for authenticity and correct any errors before publishing.
Detailed step-by-step workflow
1. Write an Instagram caption with local hashtags; three short WhatsApp Status messages; a respectful
broadcast only to customers who saved the number; a Google Business offer post and replies to reviews.
2. Build a weekly calendar from customer routines and revise after 2–3 weeks.
Tools, settings and practical guidance
Use the shop’s real photos in Google Business. Posting times suggested by AI are hypotheses, not guaranteed
best times.
Common mistakes and troubleshooting
Never invent reviews, buy followers or claim fake urgency. Avoid using other shops’ images as if they were
the client’s.
Practical assignment
Create a one-week calendar with platform, day, time and content for your business.
Student review checklist
Check that all business facts, prices and offers come from the owner.
Compare images and video to the original business; do not invent objects or people.
Confirm text, dates, location and spelling; obtain owner approval before posting.

price and timing]. Add 8–10 hashtags — mostly local ones ([city], [area], [type of shop])

and a few [food / service] ones. No claims like "best" or "No.1".

for the festival greeting. Max 10 words each.
2) One short broadcast message for regular customers who have saved our number — friendly,
no pressure, with our timing [opening – closing].
No fake urgency like "only today" or "last chance" unless it is true.
